::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Nov. 1871.  
**From:** Otterbourne,  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  This fragment printed in [<i>Dulce Domum</i>](other_books/otherbook_122.qmd), 245.
:::

[[To Mary Ann Moberly](people/person_1019.qmd)]

I have little hope of a contradiction;[^1]  it is the same island where they martyred the two boys before, and no one ever set his face more as a flint to meet whatever might come than [he](people/person_1155.qmd) did.  Once before it nearly happened.  How one must pray that this blood may be the seed of the Church!  The last I had heard was of a grand, crowning success of ninety-seven baptised at once at [Mota](organizations/other_150.qmd).   . .   So he has brought his sheaves with him![^2]  When I know more you shall hear, but his sisters are abroad;  I do not think they ever looked to see his face here . . .

---

[^1]: The news that Bishop Patteson had been murdered in the Santa Cruz Islands on 20 September 1871 was reported in *The Times*, 28 November 1871, 9e.
[^2]: Psalms 126:6.
